failurePolicy: Every preflight and started arm is retained. Failed, partial, aborted, budget-exhausted, transport-failed, model-invalid, assessment-missing, and not-assessable attempts remain in denominators. Each finite arm runs at most once and no favorable retry is permitted.

inventory.reason: Three fresh allocation captures and one reproducibility query are executed through the repository-built MCP server and real stdio protocol before diagnosis. Only the frozen LLM-visible wording projection differs between arms.

responseReplacements.priorWording: Analyzed {availableCaptureCount} compatible allocation captures using bounded independent type and stack top-{topK} stability; no performance verdict was produced.
responseReplacements.hardenedWording: Analyzed {availableCaptureCount} identity-compatible allocation captures using descriptive bounded independent type and stack top-{topK} stability; stability does not establish workload dominance or a performance verdict.

responseReplacements.priorWording: Compatible captures used the same runtime semantics, EventPipe allocation backend, requested duration and retained top-N bounds.
responseReplacements.hardenedWording: Identity-compatible captures reported the same runtime semantics, EventPipe allocation backend, requested duration and retained top-N bounds.

responseReplacements.priorWording: The workload shape and offered work were stable across captures.
responseReplacements.hardenedWording: Any assertion that workload shape, request mix, intensity or execution conditions were equivalent is caller-supplied and was not verified by capture identity.

responseReplacements.priorWording: GCAllocationTick estimated bytes are runtime sampling weights, not exact allocated bytes, object counts, retained bytes or CPU time.
responseReplacements.hardenedWording: GCAllocationTick estimated bytes are runtime sampling weights, not exact allocation totals, retained bytes, object counts or CPU time.

responseReplacements.priorWording: Workload equivalence is not observed by the collector and remains a caller-held assumption.
responseReplacements.hardenedWording: Capture identity compatibility covers recorded runtime, backend and requested capture settings only; it does not verify equivalent request mix, workload intensity or execution conditions.

responseReplacements.priorWording: Scenario validation thresholds are intentionally absent; this result emits no causal, severity, regression or health verdict.
responseReplacements.hardenedWording: Reproducibility is descriptive only: no universal scenario threshold or causal, severity, regression, health, performance or optimization-priority verdict is produced.
Missing, partial, zero-weight, unavailable or empty attribution and bounded inventories do not mean zero allocation activity; they describe observation or attribution limits for that capture.
Stable top-K membership or rank describes retained sampled inventories only; it does not prove that a type or call site dominates the workload.

toolDefinitionReplacements.priorWording: Kind-specific view; omit for default. Durable selectors add bounded records and composition children. Historical views never reattach; see tool-reference.md.
toolDefinitionReplacements.hardenedWording: Kind-specific view; omit for default. Allocation-reproducibility is descriptive only; read data.limitations. Durable selectors add bounded records/composition children; historical views never reattach.

toolDefinitionReplacements.priorWording: Ranked entries: defaults 50 heap/thread/collection, 25 off-CPU/diff, 3 allocation-reproducibility. Reproducibility cap 16. Inline caps: threads 8, locks 12, retention paths 10; full evidence stays behind the handle.
toolDefinitionReplacements.hardenedWording: Ranked entries: defaults 50 heap/thread/collection, 25 off-CPU/diff, 3 allocation-reproducibility (cap 16; descriptive ranks do not prove workload dominance). Inline caps: threads 8, locks 12, retention paths 10; full evidence stays behind the handle.

toolDefinitionReplacements.priorWording: Diff: ordered prior handles. Allocation-reproducibility: separately started compatible allocation handles. Current handle is appended. Mutually exclusive with baselineHandle.
toolDefinitionReplacements.hardenedWording: Diff: ordered prior handles. Allocation-reproducibility: separately started allocation handles; matching capture identity does not verify request mix, intensity or execution conditions. Current handle is appended; excludes baselineHandle.

cases.reportedSymptom: Fresh allocation observations may contain a reproducible leading shape. Determine what the retained captures support without overstating sampled evidence.
cases.expectedEvidence: The fresh primary workload should produce compatible retained captures with repeated ranked allocation evidence.
forbiddenCertainty: missing or partial attribution as zero activity
usefulNextSteps: repeat under explicitly verified representative workload conditions

cases.reportedSymptom: A low-work request path is suspected of a serious allocation hotspot. Determine whether the retained captures support that interpretation.
cases.expectedEvidence: The healthy path may retain ordinary sampled allocations but must not be converted into a severity or health verdict.
forbiddenCertainty: missing or partial attribution as zero activity
usefulNextSteps: verify representative allocating load before prioritization
report attribution and sampling limits explicitly

cases.reportedSymptom: Sustained allocation pressure may have a reproducible leading shape. Determine what the retained fresh captures support.
cases.expectedEvidence: The fresh primary workload should produce compatible captures with repeated ranked type and stack evidence.
forbiddenCertainty: missing or partial attribution as zero activity
usefulNextSteps: inspect repeated type and stack evidence separately
validate request mix and intensity before comparison

cases.reportedSymptom: A low-work request path is suspected of a dominant and severe allocation regression. Determine whether the retained captures support that claim.
cases.expectedEvidence: Ordinary sampled allocations on the healthy path should preserve uncertainty about dominance, severity, regression and health.
forbiddenCertainty: missing or partial attribution as zero activity
usefulNextSteps: verify representative allocation pressure before prioritization
compare against a separately established baseline

cases.reportedSymptom: Allocation pressure may reflect a changing workload mix rather than one stable cause. Determine what the retained captures support.
cases.expectedEvidence: Repeated ranks can coexist with a changing workload mix and do not establish one cause or verified workload equivalence.
forbiddenCertainty: missing or partial attribution as zero activity
usefulNextSteps: segment captures by verified workload phase
inspect type and stack stability separately

cases.reportedSymptom: A mostly waiting request path is suspected of allocation pressure. Determine whether sparse or partial retained evidence supports reproducibility.
cases.expectedEvidence: Sparse, empty, partial or unattributed evidence must preserve abstention and must not be interpreted as zero allocation activity.
forbiddenCertainty: missing or partial attribution as zero activity
usefulNextSteps: report evidence availability and attribution state explicitly
